name: ORIA Wireless Refrigerator / Freezer Thermometer with 2 Sensors
summary: A remote display and two sensors for checking refrigerated and frozen storage during an outage. Reported alarms and min/max readings support monitoring; they do not establish food safety.
description: A separate temperature display can make it easier to check cold storage without repeatedly opening a refrigerator or freezer. The owner identifies this ORIA set as one LCD receiver with two wireless sensors, indoor temperature, alarms and min/max records. Treat those features as owner-reported until the exact Canadian revision and its instructions are corroborated. Pair and check both sensors before relying on the display, keep a backup thermometer available and follow food-safety guidance after loss of cooling. No cooling control, calibration result or safe-food guarantee is implied.

pros: A separate display can reduce the need to open a cold-storage compartment just to read a thermometer.
Two reported sensor channels can support a plan for separately monitored refrigerator and freezer spaces.
cons: The exact WA50 identifier, operating limits, accuracy and Canadian revision are not corroborated by authenticated manufacturer instructions.
A snapshot or a min/max reading does not reconstruct a continuous food-temperature history.
Wireless reception, depleted batteries or an unheard alarm can interrupt monitoring; this device does not cool food.
useCases: Plan an independent temperature check alongside either BougeRV portable refrigerator, subject to the thermometer operating limits.
Check cold-storage readings during an outage while minimizing door openings and following food-safety guidance.

confirmed.text: Health Canada advises using thermometers to check refrigerator storage at or below 4°C and freezer storage at or below −18°C. This guidance does not certify this thermometer.

safetyNotes: Keep refrigerator storage at or below 4°C and freezer storage at or below −18°C. These Health Canada targets are not verified ORIA alarm thresholds or operating ratings.
A thermometer cannot guarantee food safety, prevent spoilage or determine the full time a food has been warm. Follow official advice; when in doubt, discard unsafe food.
Confirm the delivered instructions, sensor limits, alarm behaviour and battery requirements. Test reception in the intended location and compare readings with a reliable reference thermometer.
Do not assume 1.2 V NiMH compatibility from AA/AAA size alone; the ORIA battery chemistry and voltage requirements are not corroborated. Keep equipment dry according to its actual instructions.
